body.statement: The full-count rule \(t_8\) has maximum risk \(U_8\) over all \(165\) response-type states, with equality only at \((2,0,0,6)\) and \((6,0,0,2)\). The weights defining \(\pi_8^W\) are positive and sum to one, and its Bayes risk after observing \(W\) is \(L_8\). Exact rational comparison yields \[\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\le U_8=\frac{457801172643}{7000000000000}<\frac{6541}{100000}<\frac{6578}{100000}<\frac{224641744872980943629642927781}{3414537001722982784239360000000}=L_8\le\rho_8^W.\] Therefore \(\rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}<\rho_8^W\).
body.justification: A separated rational primal-dual sandwich proves strict information value without relying on tolerances or an unattained numerical optimizer.
body.gap: Blackwell garbling yields only weak dominance, and Hull's unrestricted-estimator complete-randomization discussion remains numerical and compares designs rather than the two analyses of one fixed design.
body.consumer: Users of \(\operatorname{complete\_ra}\) with \(N=8\) learn that retaining both success counts can strictly lower worst-schedule MSE.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(T_{xy}=10^6t_8(x,y)\) be the integer matrix in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}n8\mbox{-}full\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}certificate}\).  Its largest absolute entry is \(744266<10^6\), so \(t_8\) is feasible.  For a state \(N=(a,p,q,b)\), define the integer count
\[
 c_N(x,y):=\sum_{\substack{0\leq t_a\leq a,\ 0\leq t_p\leq p,\ 0\leq t_q\leq q,\ 0\leq t_b\leq b\\
 t_a+t_p+t_q+t_b=4,\ t_p+t_b=x,\ q+b-t_q-t_b=y}}
 \binom a{t_a}\binom p{t_p}\binom q{t_q}\binom b{t_b}.
\]
Then \(K_N(x,y)=c_N(x,y)/70\), \(\sum_{x,y}c_N(x,y)=70\), and exact denominator clearing gives
\[
 R_N^{\mathrm{CR}}(t_8)=\frac{S_N}{4480000000000000},
 \qquad
 S_N:=\sum_{x,y}c_N(x,y)\{8T_{xy}-10^6(p-q)\}^2.
\]
Thus the upper certificate can be checked using integers only.  Put
\[
 M:=292992750491520=640\cdot457801172643.
\]
For \(p\geq q\), define
\(
 \delta_{p,q}=M-\max_{0\leq a\leq8-p-q}S_{(a,p,q,8-a-p-q)}
\).
Direct substitution of the binomial coefficients in the preceding displayed sum gives the exhaustive triangular table
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
p& (q,\delta_{p,q})\\ \hline
0&(0,0)\\
1&(0,25780350722816),\ (1,74633180406656)\\
2&(0,28487201038976),\ (1,101366778351616),\ (2,150726698175616)\\
3&(0,20276478648640),\ (1,103205642527616),\ (2,185543066360064),\ (3,237987455841920)\\
4&(0,1042769664),\ (1,96025992016704),\ (2,177021364878208),\ (3,255669909370880),\ (4,292992750491520)\\
5&(0,5610019299520),\ (1,88299771155200),\ (2,165931651853120),\ (3,236516348250240)\\
6&(0,747443840),\ (1,120018517677760),\ (2,195440555456000)\\
7&(0,38080886782080),\ (1,138035999899520)\\
8&(0,1293664640).
\end{array}
\]
This covers every \((p,q)\) with \(p+q\leq8\): swapping the two treatment labels sends \((a,p,q,b),(x,y),\tau_N\) to \((a,q,p,b),(y,x),-\tau_N\), while \(T_{yx}=-T_{xy}\), so \(S_{(a,p,q,b)}=S_{(a,q,p,b)}\).  In the sole zero entry \((p,q)=(0,0)\), the slacks \(M-S_{(a,0,0,8-a)}\), in order \(a=0,\ldots,8\), are
\[
 (292992750491520,269063856160640,0,323070080,698375552,
 323070080,0,269063856160640,292992750491520).
\]
Every number in the triangular table other than its first zero is positive.  Hence \(S_N\leq M\) for all \(165=\binom{11}{3}\) states, with equality only for \(N=(2,0,0,6)\) and \(N=(6,0,0,2)\).  Since
\[
 \frac{M}{4480000000000000}
 =\frac{457801172643}{7000000000000}=U_8,
\]
the full-count maximum-risk assertion follows directly from the response-type kernel.

For the difference-only lower certificate, let \(Q=10^6\) and let \(q_N\) denote the eleven displayed integer weights, so \(\pi_{8,N}^W=q_N/Q\).  They are all positive and
\[
 2(25164)+4(92977)+2(37394)+2(92573)+317830=1000000=Q.
\]
For \(j=x-y\), set \(c_N(j)=\sum_{x-y=j}c_N(x,y)\), and define the integer aggregates
\[
 \alpha_j=\sum_Nq_Nc_N(j),\qquad
 \beta_j=\sum_Nq_Nc_N(j)(p-q),\qquad
 \gamma=\sum_Nq_N(p-q)^2.
\]
Substitution into the same hypergeometric counts yields \(\gamma=15211060\) and
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r}
j&\alpha_j&\beta_j\\ \hline
-4&4686730&-27876820\\
-3&6696400&-29975170\\
-2&10482010&-27731530\\
-1&7413920&-9297700\\
0&11441880&0\\
1&7413920&9297700\\
2&10482010&27731530\\
3&6696400&29975170\\
4&4686730&27876820.
\end{array}
\]
The check \(\sum_j\alpha_j=70000000=70Q\) verifies total predictive mass one, and every \(\alpha_j\) is positive.  Since \(W=2j\) and \(\tau_N=(p-q)/8\), the Bayes-dual quantities are
\[
 A_j^{\pi_8^W}=\frac{\alpha_j}{70Q},\qquad
 B_j^{\pi_8^W}=\frac{\beta_j}{560Q},\qquad
 \sum_N\pi_{8,N}^W\tau_N^2=\frac{\gamma}{64Q}.
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\mbox{-}bayes\mbox{-}dual}\) and exact square completion therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal B_W(\pi_8^W)
 &=\frac{15211060}{64\cdot10^6}
   -\sum_{j=-4}^4\frac{\beta_j^2}{64\cdot70\cdot10^6\alpha_j}\\
 &=\frac{224641744872980943629642927781}
 {3414537001722982784239360000000}=L_8.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is a legal prior lower bound for every \(W\)-measurable rule.  Finally, all three strict comparisons are certified by
\[
 \frac{6541}{100000}-U_8
 =\frac{68827357}{7000000000000}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{6578}{100000}-\frac{6541}{100000}=\frac{37}{100000}>0,
\]
and
\[
 L_8-\frac{6578}{100000}
 =\frac{33500899643136082377826981}
 {3414537001722982784239360000000}>0.
\]
The primal and dual bounds from Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}response\mbox{-}type\mbox{-}minimax\mbox{-}games}\) now yield exactly
\[
 \rho_8^{\mathrm{CR}}\leq U_8<\frac{6541}{100000}
 <\frac{6578}{100000}<L_8\leq\rho_8^W,
\]
and hence strict separation.
